message.content:
Build "team area-based access" for the Nxeon customer portal at /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, Prisma, TypeScript). Organizations + Memberships already exist; add per-member access to specific dashboard areas.

SCHEMA (already added, client generated — do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma): `Membership` now has `areas Json?` — a string[] of allowed dashboard-area keys (null = full access per the member's role). Roles are OWNER/ADMIN/MEMBER/BILLING.

FIRST read to learn patterns: lib/actions-teams.ts (existing team actions), app/dashboard/team/page.tsx (existing team UI), lib/auth.ts (requireUser), components/ui/primitives.tsx (dashboard UI: PageHeader, cards), app/dashboard/layout.tsx (the customer nav — see how sections are listed), and grep the dashboard routes under app/dashboard/ to enumerate the real areas (servers, billing, domains, email, volumes, team, settings, etc.).

BUILD:
1. **lib/team-areas.ts** (plain module, NOT "use server"): export the canonical list of assignable dashboard areas (key + label, e.g. `servers`, `billing`, `domains`, `email`, `volumes`, `support`), and a helper `memberCanAccess(membership, areaKey): boolean` (OWNER/ADMIN always true; else if `areas` is null → allow all, else membership.areas must include the key).
2. **lib/actions-teams.ts** (EXISTING "use server" — extend it, only async exports): add `setMemberAreas(membershipId, areas: string[])` — OWNER/ADMIN only, validates the actor's membership + that target isn't an owner; persist to Membership.areas. Keep existing exports intact.
3. **app/dashboard/team/page.tsx** (extend): in the member list, add a per-member area editor (a set of toggle checkboxes from lib/team-areas.ts) that calls setMemberAreas via a small client component you create (components/customer/MemberAreas.tsx). Owners/admins see full access (not editable).
4. **Enforcement**: create a helper the dashboard can use so a member acting within an org only sees/reaches their allowed areas. Add a note (comment) at the top of app/dashboard/layout.tsx describing where to call `memberCanAccess` to hide nav items — but DO NOT edit app/dashboard/layout.tsx yourself (the orchestrator wires nav). If there's a natural per-page guard pattern, expose a `requireArea`-style helper in lib/team-areas.ts for pages to call.

RULES: "use server" files export only async functions. Do NOT edit: prisma/schema.prisma, app/dashboard/layout.tsx, worker/*, lib/rbac.ts (that's admin RBAC, different). Do NOT run build/tsc/prisma/commit. Enforce ownership/roles on every action. Match existing code style.

Report each file created/edited, the area keys you defined, and exactly where the orchestrator should add nav-hiding in app/dashboard/layout.tsx.

1	import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
2	import type { Role, User } from "@prisma/client";
3	import { realUser } from "./auth";

5	/**
6	 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
7	 *
8	 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
9	 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
10	 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav
11	 * items a role can't reach; each sensitive page additionally gates itself with
12	 * `requireArea(...)` so a hand-typed URL is refused too.
13	 */
14	export type Area =
15	  | "overview"
16	  | "analytics"
17	  | "clients"
18	  | "support"
19	  | "fleet"
20	  | "billing"
21	  | "platform";
22	
23	/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
24	export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
25	  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
26	  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
27	  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
28	  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
29	  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
30	  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
31	  platform: ["ADMIN"],
32	};
33	
34	export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
35	  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);
36	}
37	
38	/** Any non-customer role that belongs in the ops portal. */
39	export function isStaff(role: Role): boolean {
40	  return role === "SUPPORT" || role === "BILLING" || role === "ADMIN";
41	}
42	
43	/** Maps admin nav hrefs to their governing area. Unknown routes default to platform (ADMIN-only). */

91	/**
92	 * Server-side page guard. Redirects to /login if signed out, or back to the
93	 * overview if the (staff) user's role can't reach this area. Returns the real
94	 * signed-in user (impersonation is refused elsewhere in the admin layout).
95	 */
96	export async function requireArea(area: Area): Promise<User> {
97	  const user = await realUser();
98	  if (!user) redirect("/login");
99	  if (!isStaff(user.role)) redirect("/dashboard");
100	  if (!canAccess(user.role, area)) redirect("/admin");
101	  return user;
102	}

model Organization {
  id        String       @id @default(cuid())
  name      String
  ownerId   String
  owner     User         @relation("OrgOwner", fields: [ownerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  members   Membership[]
  createdAt DateTime     @default(now())
}
model Membership {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  orgId     String
  org       Organization @relation(fields: [orgId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  userId    String
  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  role      String   @default("MEMBER") // OWNER | ADMIN | MEMBER | BILLING
  areas     Json?    // per-member allowed dashboard areas (null = role default); string[] of area keys
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@unique([orgId, userId])
}

I think the intent is to document where this logic should go rather than actually modifying the file.

I'll load the membership by ID, verify the actor has OWNER or ADMIN permissions in that org, confirm the target member isn't an owner, and validate the areas being assigned.

I'm importing the area validation helpers from lib/team-areas into the server actions file, which is fine since team-areas is just a plain utility module. I'll filter the areas to valid keys, deduplicate them, and allow an empty array (which means the member has no access to restricted areas) — that's a valid state. Then I'll persist the changes and return a response object with error or success status.

Now I'm building out the MemberAreas client component and integrating it into the page layout. I'll render the MemberAreas component as an expandable section below each member's role, showing area toggles for non-owner members and "Full access" for owners and admins. The component needs membershipId, initial areas, and an editable flag to handle the toggle logic and API calls. When areas is null, I'll show all checkboxes as checked to represent the full access default, but I need to handle what happens when an admin unchecks some—that sends an explicit list of remaining areas. To restore full access, they'd just check all boxes again, which effectively gives the same result as null. For areas not in DASHBOARD_AREAS, I'll need to account for those edge cases in the access logic.

For OWNER and ADMIN members who can't edit their areas, I'll display a "Full access" badge instead of the checkbox component. Now I'm ready to start building the team-areas utility file.
